51204971.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal 6xHis-tagged human recombinant FGFR1 (458 to 765) by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51204971.references_previous: Norman, R. A.; Schott, A.-K.; Andrews, D. M.; Breed, J.; Foote, K. M.; Garner, A. P.; Ogg, D.; Orme, J. P.; Pink, J. H.; Roberts, K.; Rudge, D. A.; Thomas, A. P.; Leach, A. G. Protein-ligand crystal structures can guide the design of selective inhibitors of the FGFR tyrosine kinase. J. Med. Chem. 2012, 55, 5003–12.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) using N-terminal 6xHis-tagged human recombinant FGFR1 (458 to 765) immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip via amine coupling. The immobilization level was approximately 1000 response units (RU). The running buffer was HBS-EP+ (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20). The inhibitors were dissolved in DMSO and diluted in running buffer to concentrations ranging from 0.1 nM to 10 μM. The association phase lasted 120 s, followed by a 120 s dissociation phase. Regeneration was achieved with 10 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.0, for 30 s. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The binding affinity (KD) was determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model. The SPR data were collected at 25 °C. The SPR experiments were performed as described previously (8).

analyte.description: Inhibitors (dissolved in DMSO and diluted in running buffer)

assay_conditions.running_buffer_composition: HBS-EP+ (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20)
